assertions_contracts.best_practice: C++26 Contracts are the designated successor facility: GCC's status page lists Contracts (P2900R14) as available in GCC 16, while Clang's status page still lists them as not implemented; libc++ hardening assertion semantics are explicitly modelled on C++26 Contracts evaluation semantics.
assertions_contracts.evidence: Fresh text check: the guide contains no contracts migration note (its only C++26 mention in Sec.2 is a warning not to describe C++26 features as C++23 guarantees). The run-1 proposal was not applied (FINDINGS pass-2 'What remains open' leaves proposals unapplied), so the gap is unchanged, now with GCC 16 support strengthening the watch item.
assertions_contracts.guide_position: static_assert for compile-time facts, assert() for runtime invariants (NDEBUG caveat stated), no side effects inside assertions, span treated as a borrow not a bounds check; no contract facility and no C++26 contracts migration note, because the guide targets C++23.

bounded_work.best_practice: The direction of the standard validates the philosophy: C++26 adds std::inplace_vector, a fixed-capacity contiguous container with storage inside the object - exactly the bounded-storage shape this guide hand-rolls under C++23 - and libstdc++ has added it for C++26.
bounded_work.evidence: Fresh text check: std::inplace_vector is never mentioned in SKILL.md or the full guide (grep: 0 occurrences). Nothing official contradicts explicit budgets; the improvement is an unmentioned standard facility, so the run-1 verdict stands.
bounded_work.guide_position: Named constexpr budgets for counts, bytes, depth, retries and queues; growth and reserve() bounded before allocation; retries need idempotency and a shared deadline.

concurrency.best_practice: jthread + stop_token remains the sanctioned owned-thread model. C++26 adds std::execution, hazard pointers and RCU upstream, but Clang's status page still shows the C++2c line as only Partial, so none of it displaces the guide's portable ownership/cancellation discipline today.
concurrency.evidence: Clang C++ status page fetched 2026-10-14: C++2c Partial; the guide's position is unchanged in the current text and uncontradicted.
concurrency.guide_position: Prefer std::jthread with an explicit cooperative stop-token protocol; data races are UB; volatile does not synchronise; coroutine frames need a named owner; bounded task count and queues.

error_handling.best_practice: std::expected is the standard C++23 vocabulary for expected failure and remains so heading into C++26; the C++ Core Guidelines sanction both exceptions for non-locally-handled errors and expected-style returns under a documented per-codebase policy, which is what the guide mandates.
error_handling.evidence: Guide Sec.7 and Sec.41 [X1][X2] cite the draft expected specification and the Core Guidelines directly; no fetched 2026 source changes that model.
error_handling.guide_position: One exception policy plus one typed expected-error policy per subsystem; std::expected<T,E> for routine domain failure, checked before value/error access; no exception crosses a C ABI boundary; exception guarantees documented.

formatting.best_practice: clang-format remains the reference formatter for C++ and the four pinned options are current documented style options. The values are house policy (the LLVM preset itself uses different defaults), which the guide presents as its own pin, not an upstream claim.
formatting.evidence: Current LLVM documentation fetched 2026-10-14 still documents the clang-format style mechanism and the LLVM preset the pin is based on; guide Sec.23 text is unchanged and accurate.
formatting.guide_position: Pinned clang-format: BasedOnStyle LLVM, IndentWidth 4, ColumnLimit 100, UseTab Never; headers self-contained; semantic rewrites run separately from formatting.

memory_ownership.best_practice: The C++ Core Guidelines' resource-management rules still prescribe exactly this model: RAII, unique ownership by default, shared ownership only for genuine sharing, no raw owning pointers or new/delete in application code, with tool enforcement.
memory_ownership.evidence: Guide Sec.14/Sec.26 restate that model and cite the Core Guidelines [X2] as their source; C++26 hardening/erroneous-behaviour work reinforces rather than replaces it.
memory_ownership.guide_position: RAII and Rule of Zero; unique_ptr for exclusive ownership, shared_ptr only for genuine shared ownership, cycles broken deliberately; nonthrowing destructors; explicit checked finish for fallible completion; views borrow and never extend lifetime.

security.best_practice: Standard-library hardening is a first-class vendor-documented defence: libc++ offers none/fast/extensive/debug modes, its docs recommend fast for most production projects, the vendor default is none, and production-mode failures trap immediately.
security.evidence: Fresh text check: neither SKILL.md nor the full guide names a hardening mode or the _LIBCPP_HARDENING_MODE macro (grep: 0 occurrences); Sec.18/Sec.27 still tell a sanitizer-only runtime story. The run-1 proposal was not applied, so the verdict stands on the freshly fetched hardening page.
security.guide_position: Warnings plus ASan/UBSan in testing, review of casts/pointers/format strings/dynamic loading as trust boundaries, no std::system on external input, argv form; no standard-library hardening mode is named in the profile declaration or the build recipes.

static_analysis.best_practice: clang-tidy is the official enforcement vehicle: its docs list cppcoreguidelines- checks that mechanically enforce the Core Guidelines, cert- checks for CERT, bugprone- checks for the lifetime/view mistakes this guide warns about, and it also runs the Clang Static Analyzer checks.
static_analysis.evidence: clang-tidy page fetched 2026-10-14 lists all of those check groups. Fresh text check: 'clang-tidy' occurs 0 times in the guide, so the run-1 gap and verdict are unchanged.
static_analysis.guide_position: SKILL pairing is clangd + clang-format + lldb-dap; the full guide (Sec.18) says to use warnings, sanitizers and static analysis together but names no analyzer, no check set and no CI step.

testing.best_practice: Consistent with Core Guidelines and sanitizer practice; current libc++ guidance adds the debug hardening mode for test suites, CI and local development as a complement, which is scored as a proposal under security rather than a defect in this test matrix.
testing.evidence: Guide Sec.28 text is unchanged; the fetched hardening page confirms debug mode's intended test/CI role without superseding any guide test rule.
testing.guide_position: Expected-error alternatives, empty/max views, sanitizer-driven lifetime tests, allocation/constructor failure, output preservation, exception guarantees, cancellation/destructor-join tests, release (NDEBUG) run with independent checks.

toolchain_pins.best_practice: C++23 remains the current published ISO standard on isocpp.org (ISO/IEC 14882:2024); C++26 is still in-progress material there and only Partial in Clang / experimental in GCC, so a C++23 pin is current, with contracts/reflection as the dated migration horizon.
toolchain_pins.evidence: isocpp.org 'The Standard' page fetched 2026-10-14 names C++23 as the current standard; Clang's status page confirms Partial C++2c support with Contracts and Reflection unimplemented. No remediation was needed for this aspect in pass 2 and none was claimed.
toolchain_pins.guide_position: C++23 is the reference profile (std::expected); C++20 projects must supply an alternative result type; C++26 features must not be described as C++23 guarantees.
